metadata.name: Software Development Flow
metadata.description: Implements one complete repository change through source-grounded requirements, independently reviewed development-only planning, repository-grounded vertical units, fresh producer completion, cause-aware repair and versioned replan. Its always-visible seven-stage progress graph and matching PNG keep stable inactive milestones while the exact current node truthfully names the active unit, iteration, validation, independent review, repair, checkpoint or finalization role. Existing authorized Telegram attention may attach that same image without changing routing or authority. Caller-owned follow-ups remain durable completion reminders rather than development work. Each plan unit owns code, tests, permanent documentation and applicable runtime evidence; push, pull request, publication, release and deployment remain caller or parent-process effects.

nodes.directive:
Capture the user's development task and authority before task-specific discovery or repository mutation. Read all standing project instructions. Create ./moira-ws/software-development-flow-{task-name}-{YYYYMMDD}-{HHMM}/ and treat it as the new workspace throughout this directive; do not use workspace_path before returning it. Inside that workspace, write this execution ID to process-id.txt and keep task-requirements.md as the single canonical requirements source. Resolve every explicitly assigned ticket, pull request, issue, specification, or document through available project-native mechanisms; preserve its identity, retrieval location, and complete current content in durable source files without preliminary relevance filtering, then separately incorporate all authoritative requirements without reducing them to a lossy summary. If a source cannot be obtained, expose that blocker instead of planning without it. Before mutation, inspect project-native VCS read-only and record VCS kind, branch or bookmark, status, relevant diff/baseline, unrelated changes to preserve, and already authorized side effects in vcs-baseline.md without assuming Git or requiring a clean tree. Discover task-relevant entry points, interfaces and data flow, implementations, dependencies and consumers, tests and fixtures, coverage policy/maps, documentation, configuration and schemas, generated artifacts, project-native commands, build/environment/health, runtime/integration surfaces, UI/browser architecture, CI/review/checklists, ownership boundaries, and applicable security/performance constraints. Record exact locations/evidence or a justified N/A in project-context.md. Use additional project-native searches when one search is insufficient; never conclude that an artifact or dependency does not exist from one superficial search. Ask only for a material fact that cannot be discovered. Do not create permanent guides merely because one is absent, and do not mutate the repository here. Return the new workspace path as workspace_path.

Resolve `operating_mode` in this same turn: reuse a mode the user already stated; infer an unambiguous one, including a run started by an already autonomous parent process; otherwise ask once, naming the consequence — in `autonomous` there are no intermediate approvals of requirements, plan, units, or result, only the final report, while `interactive` keeps every current approval. The mode holds for the whole run and is never asked again.

Resolve visual_validation_preference in this same turn before planning. Reuse an explicit user choice. When the task context does not determine it, recommend the proportionate value, ask one simple question with disabled, screenshots, and html_report, and explain that exact units can still be refined during interactive plan approval. This preference guides plan construction only; the current reviewed plan becomes the sole runtime source of each unit policy.

When the originating request already authorizes a later push, pull request, publication, release, deployment, or another caller-owned effect after development, preserve it in canonical requirements as caller-owned downstream intent without adding it to development plan units. Query this execution's reminders through `session({ action: "reminders", executionId })` to obtain the current revision, then add one durable reminder through `session({ action: "add-reminder", executionId, reminderText, idempotencyKey, expectedRevision })`. State the concrete requested next action and its existing authority; use a stable idempotency key for retries. Do this for standalone and child executions alike. A reminder neither performs nor authorizes the effect, changes no development plan or `vcs_commits_authorized`, and appears only in the normal completion response as a requested next action.
nodes.completionCondition: Task, authority, assigned sources, canonical requirements, read-only VCS baseline, operating mode, visual preference, correlated workspace, and relevant project context are durably captured before mutation; every already-authorized caller-owned follow-up is stored as an active execution reminder without becoming development work or authority

nodes.directive: Present the complete current requirements at {{workspace_path}}/task-requirements.md and ask whether they accurately capture the task, constraints, authority, and acceptance criteria. Read the file when exact current content is not already available or may have changed. Do not edit it here. On rejection, save the user's verbatim feedback to {{workspace_path}}/requirements-feedback.md.
nodes.completionCondition: The user approved the current requirements or supplied actionable feedback

nodes.directive: Use the verbatim feedback in {{workspace_path}}/requirements-feedback.md to update {{workspace_path}}/task-requirements.md. Preserve every unaffected requirement and authority boundary, resolve conflicts with the user when necessary, and keep one canonical requirements source. Do not create a parallel summary.
nodes.completionCondition: Canonical requirements incorporate the feedback without losing unaffected requirements

nodes.directive: Determine whether initial project-health evidence is relevant to the approved task. Use project-native instructions and the task-relevant context already captured; a missing guide is not permission to skip applicable checks. When relevant, run the smallest startup and baseline-test checks that establish a truthful starting state. Write {{workspace_path}}/project-health.md with exact commands, outcomes, and classification. Distinguish a healthy state, inapplicability, unrelated pre-existing failure, repository failure that this task must resolve before development, and an external blocker requiring changed state.
nodes.completionCondition: Applicable baseline evidence and a truthful classified outcome exist in project-health.md

nodes.directive:
Present the external blocker from {{workspace_path}}/project-health.md. Ask the user to confirm that external state changed before retrying, or to abort. Do not retry on an unchanged environment. If aborting, ensure the health report contains the current blocker and partial-work facts.

In `autonomous` mode do not ask: re-check the external state yourself and retry only on evidence that it actually changed; otherwise abort with the blocker and partial-work facts recorded.
nodes.completionCondition: The user confirmed changed external state or chose to abort

nodes.directive:
Create the current material plan revision at {{workspace_path}}/plans/{{plan_revision}}/plan.md from the canonical requirements, resolved assigned sources, task-relevant project evidence, VCS baseline, and actual repository contracts. Define independently completable outcome-oriented units with affected responsibilities and boundaries, dependencies and ordering, contracts and invariants, observable acceptance evidence, expected task-owned files, applicable tests and coverage-map updates, permanent documentation, security/performance/runtime/UI obligations, risks, and unresolved decisions. Map every affected or at-risk behavior to automated evidence or a justified manual check. Give every unit one explicit visualMode value — disabled, screenshots, or html_report — and one userApproval boolean. html_report includes the same screenshot capture and actual inspection as screenshots and never creates a second capture pass. In autonomous mode every userApproval is false. Apply visual_validation_preference proportionately; in interactive mode the user may refine exact unit policies during plan approval. Record the requested project-native authority for checkpoint commits after accepted units and final reconciliation. Preserve executor freedom over exploration, decomposition details, tools, edit order, and repair tactics unless a real external contract constrains them.

Follow `{{workspace_path}}/standards/planning.md`; the path is canonical and unchanged content need not be reread when already present and certain.

Before making an acceptance mechanism contractual, name the required state, a plausible wrong state that can look similar, and the observation that reliably differs; match mechanical, behavioral, semantic, architectural, or user evidence to the property. If the observation is compatible with both states, revise the criterion or evidence method before implementation. Require each unit's producer to own every foreseeable consequence of its complete outcome before review. Treat expected files only as known ownership or external-contract boundaries, never an exhaustive implementation whitelist. Do not create a validation-only unit unless validation itself is the requested result with a consumer and distinguishing output.

A unit fixes an outcome, its acceptance evidence, and what it depends on; it does not carry the deliverable itself. The test that holds in any medium: after the plan is approved, work an intelligent executor still has to do remains, and a unit a later step could satisfy by copying text out of the plan is a unit whose result is already written here.`standards/planning.md` states this in full.
Closed units stay as they were closed and keep the index they were closed at: a unit report lives at a path addressed by that index, so a revision that shifts a closed unit makes a later executor overwrite another unit's account.

This is a repository development plan. It may own implementation, tests, permanent documentation, generated or executable consequences, validation, review, and authorized project-native local commits or checkpoints. It must not create units for push, pull request creation or merge, publication, release, or deployment. Keep any already authorized downstream delivery intent visible for the caller or parent in the final report. Verify that every caller-owned follow-up from intake already has an active execution reminder; if a newly clarified authorized follow-up appears here, record it through the same revisioned `session` reminder API before completing this step. Do not copy reminder items into the development plan, treat reminder storage as execution or authority, or assume a parent execution exists.
nodes.completionCondition: A complete outcome-oriented current development plan exists; every unit has valid visualMode and userApproval, discriminating evidence, producer-owned code/tests/documentation completeness, dependencies, and stable closed-unit origins; push, PR, publication, release, and deployment are excluded from units and every already-authorized caller-owned follow-up remains an active execution reminder

nodes.directive:
Review {{workspace_path}}/plans/{{plan_revision}}/plan.md independently against the complete canonical requirements, every assigned primary source, standing project instructions, relevant repository architecture and behavior, VCS/side-effect boundaries, and prior completed work. Use a separate reviewer context or subagent when the host supports it; otherwise perform a fresh self-review and disclose that fallback in the report. Read primary artifacts directly when they are not already available or may have changed. Verify requirements coverage, dependencies, writer/reader contracts, executable routes, test and documentation obligations, task-file ownership, checkpoint authority, and observable evidence. When prior completed work is carried forward, verify that every accepted outcome names its originating plan revision and unit index and that cited evidence resolves under that origin; do not accept current array position as proof of origin. Verify the evidence required by each unit's explicit visualMode and the originating task without silently elevating the current reviewed plan from screenshots to html_report or from disabled to another mode. Overwrite {{workspace_path}}/plans/{{plan_revision}}/review.md with the findings, as the review standard requires. Do not block on formatting taste, fixed step counts, or speculative redesign.

The review subject is this plan for the original task, not the whole product. Use surrounding code and architecture only to judge whether the plan can satisfy the original requirements and preserve affected contracts. Do not invent requirements or widen the task. This boundary does not protect an inadequate plan: when evidence shows that the proposed plan or architecture cannot correctly deliver an original requirement, report the defect and require the plan to change within the original task. If the evidence would require changing the original task boundary itself, report that decision explicitly for the user instead of silently expanding it.

Do not run linters, type checks, test suites, builds, or other mechanical checks during review. Consume current evidence already produced for those properties and spend the review on semantic, architectural, and planning judgement.

Judge the plan by `{{workspace_path}}/standards/planning.md` and conduct the review by `{{workspace_path}}/standards/review.md`; both paths are canonical and unchanged content need not be reread when already present and certain. A standard that does not apply to this change is met.

Before selecting the route, classify each confirmed finding by its earliest cause: product defect, test or validation defect, insufficient existing evidence, documentation or process projection, invalid or undemonstrable criterion, or upstream requirements, plan, or process defect. State the aggregate disposition in the same current report. Return only `review_outcome`: `pass` when there are no blockers; `repair` only when every blocker is owned by this review's paired repair responsibility and its upstream contract remains sound; `replan` when any blocker invalidates a criterion, evidence model, architecture decision, plan, requirements interpretation, or process. Mixed causes return `replan`. Do not return a count.

Verify that every unit has exactly one valid visualMode and userApproval, that html_report inherently includes one screenshot validation pass, and that autonomous units all disable user approval. Reject any unit for push, pull request, publication, release, or deployment. Confirm that the intake visual preference guided planning but does not remain a runtime source beside the current plan.
nodes.completionCondition: Current plan review is complete, cause-classified, scoped to the original task, and review_outcome matches pass, repair, or replan

nodes.directive:
Repair the current plan revision using {{workspace_path}}/plans/{{plan_revision}}/review.md. Reproduce each blocking defect, correct the root cause in the plan, preserve still-valid decisions and executor freedom, and update the same plan artifact. Do not implement style suggestions or create review bookkeeping.

Repair against `{{workspace_path}}/standards/planning.md` and `{{workspace_path}}/standards/review.md`.

Before mutation classify every finding by earliest cause and inspect the current review for a returning root. Return `repair_outcome=replan` without changing the plan when the upstream requirements interpretation, architecture, criterion, or evidence model is invalid, the finding cannot be reproduced, the proposed observation cannot distinguish the required state, or the same root returned without stronger relevant knowledge. Return `repair_outcome=changed` only after a coherent plan-owned correction that preserves the original goal and all unaffected decisions.

Persist a `replan` diagnosis to {{workspace_path}}/plans/{{plan_revision}}/repair.md as this substantive repair owner's current evidence; the plan revision owner consumes that fixed path together with the current review. Do not create it for an ordinary changed repair.
Closed units stay as they were closed and keep the index they were closed at: a unit report lives at a path addressed by that index, so a revision that shifts a closed unit makes a later executor overwrite another unit's account.

When the finding cannot be corrected without touching a closed unit, that is a cause above repair: return `repair_outcome=replan` without mutating the plan, so unit closure and a new plan revision decide it in the open. Do not stop the run in place of that route.
nodes.completionCondition: Plan findings are reproduced and cause-classified; the plan either changed coherently or replan was selected before invalid mutation, and closed units keep both their content and the index they were closed at, and every unit it shapes fixes what must become true, the evidence that would accept it, and what it depends on rather than carrying the deliverable

nodes.directive: Present the complete independently reviewed current plan revision at {{workspace_path}}/plans/{{plan_revision}}/plan.md, including architecture, outcomes, dependencies, each unit's visualMode and userApproval, evidence obligations, risks, local VCS boundary, and caller/parent delivery follow-up. When completed outcomes are carried forward, present their originating revision and unit index. Ask only whether the user approves this plan. Plan approval cannot grant, revoke, or transport VCS authority. On rejection, save verbatim feedback to {{workspace_path}}/plans/{{plan_revision}}/user-feedback.md. Do not derive cursor or unit count, edit the plan, change authority records, mutate the repository, or touch VCS here.
nodes.completionCondition: The interactive user approved the exact reviewed plan or supplied actionable verbatim rejection feedback, without changing VCS authority or deriving execution cursor state

nodes.directive:

The engine has already advanced the revision number; do not renumber it. Preserve the rejected revision where it stands, carry forward unaffected requirements and completed work, and do not create a summary relay. For every accepted completed outcome carried forward, record its exact originating plan revision and originating unit index and cite evidence beneath that origin; never relabel it as evidence of its new array position.

Follow `{{workspace_path}}/standards/planning.md`.
Closed units stay as they were closed and keep the index they were closed at: a unit report lives at a path addressed by that index, so a revision that shifts a closed unit makes a later executor overwrite another unit's account.
nodes.completionCondition: A new material plan revision incorporates the user's rejection feedback, and closed units keep both their content and the index they were closed at, and every unit it shapes fixes what must become true, the evidence that would accept it, and what it depends on rather than carrying the deliverable

nodes.directive:
Implement approved plan unit {{current_step_index}} of {{total_steps}} from {{workspace_path}}/plans/{{plan_revision}}/plan.md, using the complete current plan when it may have changed and the repository-grounded preparation at {{workspace_path}}/plans/{{plan_revision}}/step-{{current_step_index}}/implementation-preparation.md. Own the complete approved vertical outcome: inspect real dependencies and surrounding contracts, change the repository, preserve unrelated work, add or update necessary tests and coverage artifacts, update applicable permanent documentation, and complete configuration, schemas, migrations, generated output, runtime/integration behavior, and applicable security, performance or UI obligations. Run useful focused checks. Do not intentionally defer a known artifact class or integration consequence to the completion turn.

Write the unit's initial account to {{workspace_path}}/plans/{{plan_revision}}/step-{{current_step_index}}/unit-report.md in this turn. It is the account of the unit, not of your turn: state what the unit now delivers and the evidence for it — task-owned files, commands and outcomes, behavior/evidence mappings, documentation impact — together with which earlier behavior the change could have disturbed, unresolved facts, and unrelated changes that remain excluded. Carry decisive output instead of prose retelling. Later responsibilities that change the unit leave this same account true, so write present state rather than round history. Open it with the unit baseline in one line: the previous-unit checkpoint where project version control provides one, the state in {{workspace_path}}/vcs-baseline.md for the first unit, otherwise repository state at the start of this unit. Do not commit or publish here.

Work to {{workspace_path}}/standards/engineering.md and {{workspace_path}}/standards/tests.md; when permanent documentation is affected, also use {{workspace_path}}/standards/documentation.md. The paths are canonical and unchanged content need not be reread when already present and certain. Where surrounding code is wrong, implement correctly, say where you diverged, and report the defect rather than repairing unrelated areas. Before adding or elevating validation machinery, name the required and plausible wrong states and use it only when its observation differs or it is itself the requested result with a consumer. Do not create a mechanism whose purpose is proving that another check ran.

Keep the unit account explicit about every affected permanent documentation file and its current reproducible evidence. Documentation is part of the vertical result, not work deferred to final reconciliation.
nodes.completionCondition: The complete approved vertical unit, its initial truthful account, applicable tests and documentation, and focused evidence exist before the fresh producer completion pass

nodes.directive:
Inspect the actual repository changes for plan unit {{current_step_index}}, standing project instructions, the approved outcome, the current unit account at {{workspace_path}}/plans/{{plan_revision}}/step-{{current_step_index}}/unit-report.md, and the record of the round just closed at {{workspace_path}}/plans/{{plan_revision}}/step-{{current_step_index}}/iteration-{{previous_iteration}}/repair.md when this is not the unit's first pass. Run the smallest applicable project-native deterministic checks that diagnose the affected scope; this mechanical gate does not require a separate reviewer context. Use formatting, lint, static analysis, scoped type checking or compilation, targeted tests, generated-output consistency, explicit registry/schema/identifier checks, and project checklists only where their established output observes a relevant current property. Record exact commands, outcomes, current versus stale evidence, and every reproducible repository defect by overwriting {{workspace_path}}/plans/{{plan_revision}}/step-{{current_step_index}}/iteration-{{current_iteration}}/cheap-validation.md. Do not rerun broad checks whose evidence the latest mutation could not invalidate, and do not treat unrelated or external failures as success. Return only the exact blocking issue count.

The subject is the unit as it now stands against the baseline line in unit-report.md, not only the latest repair diff. This gate does not decide semantic completeness of scenarios, tests, documentation, business contracts, migrations, concurrency treatment, infrastructure or product meaning. Producer completion and the applicable semantic review own those judgments. A deterministic check for such an area belongs here only when its observation actually distinguishes the relevant states. Before adding or newly elevating a validator, harness, adapter, proxy, guard, scanner, coverage mechanism or metatest, or when a signal's applicability is disputed, name the required state, a plausible wrong state and the observation that differs. If no observation differs, do not create surrogate proof. Established project-native lint, type, compile, format and targeted-test commands rely on their existing contracts and need no repeated proof-model recital.

The linter, type system and compiler are what run here; tests are not substitutes for them, and a test that asserts only what those tools already guarantee adds maintenance without protection.
nodes.completionCondition: Current deterministic evidence covers every applicable mechanically observable property and the issue count matches reproducible repository defects without claiming semantic completeness

nodes.directive:
Use the current cheap-validation report to reproduce and repair every repository-caused blocking defect at its root. Preserve unrelated changes and do not absorb unrelated or external failures. Never obtain a pass by weakening tests, assertions, schemas, types, lint, coverage, or another quality gate; change a validator or test only with concrete proof that its expectation is obsolete. Do not add sleeps, force, blind retries, swallowed errors, suppression, or timeout inflation. Record this correction in {{workspace_path}}/plans/{{plan_revision}}/step-{{current_step_index}}/iteration-{{current_iteration}}/repair.md, the record of the round you are closing: what you changed, which earlier behaviour of the unit that could have disturbed, and the evidence for the repair itself, added to whatever an earlier correction of this same round already recorded, and run focused evidence before independent revalidation.

When this correction changed the unit, bring the unit's account at {{workspace_path}}/plans/{{plan_revision}}/step-{{current_step_index}}/unit-report.md to what the unit now is, in this same turn: you are its current owner, so rewrite what your change made untrue rather than appending a section about this round.

Repair against `{{workspace_path}}/standards/review.md`.

Before changing the repository, reproduce the finding and classify its earliest cause. Inspect the current repair record for the same root class. If the artifact this node may change does not own the cause, the proposed evidence cannot distinguish the required state, the same root returned without a changed source of truth, external fact, distinguishing observation, or testable hypothesis, or recent cycles changed only validation/reporting machinery while direct product evidence stayed green, do not mutate and return `repair_outcome=replan`. Validation infrastructure is exempt from the drift diagnosis only when it is itself the requested result with a consumer and distinguishing output.

For a changed repair, bound class-wide work to real manifestations of a reproduced root inside the original task. Use mechanical regression evidence only when it distinguishes the class states; use bounded primary-artifact inspection and review for contextual properties. Return `repair_outcome=changed` and `mutation_scope=verification_only` only when changes stay in tests, fixtures, coverage evidence, or verification specifications while product behavior, contracts, schemas, configuration, generated behavior, architecture, and test intent remain unchanged and focused checks pass. Return `mutation_scope=product` for any wider change or incomplete check.

When returning `replan` without mutation, write the current cause, unchanged-repository evidence, and `replan` disposition to {{workspace_path}}/plans/{{plan_revision}}/step-{{current_step_index}}/iteration-{{current_iteration}}/repair.md. This is the existing repair owner's evidence consumed by unit closure and plan revision, not a relay or second findings report.
nodes.completionCondition: Cheap-validation defects are reproduced and cause-classified; changed repair states actual verification-only or product scope, or replans before invalid mutation

Inspect changed and at-risk behavior, boundaries, contracts, schemas, configuration, integrations, regression risks, concurrency, migrations, and failure paths rather than using function or assertion counts. planning_standards.default:
# Planning standards

These are outcomes, not procedures. An item that does not apply to the current change is met, and
nothing needs to be produced to prove it inapplicable. Cite only what is violated; do not walk this
document item by item.

## A unit is a vertical slice

Each unit changes observable behaviour and carries, inside itself, the tests and the verification
that prove it. It crosses whatever layers it needs to do that.

*Why.* A unit whose proof lives in a later unit cannot be accepted on its own, and nothing can tell
whether it is finished. Splitting by layer instead — one unit for storage, one for the API, one for
the interface — produces work that is neither independent nor separately valuable. (INVEST; vertical
vs horizontal slicing.)

## No unit is only tests, only validation, only documentation, or only cleanup

Unless that is what the task itself asks for.

*Why.* Such a unit is an admission that the previous one was delivered unfinished, and it moves the
proof away from the work it proves. The verification that ends up in a "testing" unit is the same
verification the implementing unit needed to be acceptable.

## The plan opens with the architecture it assumes

Components, how they interact, the decisions taken, and the consequences those decisions accept.
Decisions deliberately deferred are named as deferred.

*Why.* Without it the reviewer judges steps and never the shape, and the first unit silently fixes an
architecture nobody agreed to. Consequences are the part that makes the record useful later. (ADR:
context, decision, consequences.)

## Work moves from the core outward

Data and domain logic first, then integration and interfaces, then presentation — unless a real
dependency runs the other way and the plan says which.

*Why.* Building the outer layer first freezes a contract underneath it that nothing has exercised yet.

## Each unit is readable by someone who never saw the conversation

What it produces, what it depends on, and what evidence would show it done.

*Why.* The reviewer, and often the executor, arrive without that history; anything they cannot
reconstruct becomes an assumption nobody checks.

## The plan does not enumerate files, symbols, line numbers, or pseudocode

It fixes outcomes, contracts, invariants, dependencies, acceptance evidence, and known risks.

*Why.* Naming files before the code has been read chooses tactics blindly and substitutes a false
sense of completeness for the analysis the executor still has to do. The executor has the repository
in front of it; the planner does not. (INVEST — negotiable.)

## Size follows the work

One unit is a complete plan when the task is small. A unit that needs sub-items is two units.

*Why.* Padding a plan to look thorough adds review cycles without adding work, and sub-items hide a
unit that was never independently completable.

## Every unit names the evidence that would accept it

In observable terms: a behaviour to exercise, a state to inspect, an artifact to compare.

*Why.* Acceptance criteria written as adjectives — robust, clean, complete — cannot be met or
refused, so they end up decided by whoever is more insistent.

## Unresolved decisions are named as unresolved

*Why.* An open question recorded as an assumption becomes a defect that surfaces after the work is
built on top of it.


## Acceptance evidence distinguishes the required state

Before making a check contractual, name the required state, a plausible wrong state that can look similar, and the observation that reliably differs. Match the method to the property: deterministic structure can be checked mechanically, behavior through actual behavior, semantic completeness through primary-source judgment, and architecture through contextual review. If the observation is compatible with both states, revise the criterion or evidence method before implementation rather than creating a surrogate proof.

*Why.* An executable signal that the wrong result can reproduce turns later review into repeated construction of validators for validators.

## The producer owns foreseeable completeness before review

Each unit includes every consequence discoverable from the requirements and repository contracts: behavior, dependencies, tests, documentation, generated output, runtime, security, performance, compatibility, and operations as applicable. Review independently challenges that outcome; it is not the normal place where the plan first remembers an obvious obligation.

*Why.* A local checklist item can be green while its complete product outcome is still unfinished.

## Validation remains subordinate unless it is the requested result

Validation infrastructure is a legitimate unit when the user requested it, it has a real consumer, and its output distinguishes relevant states. Otherwise it is supporting evidence inside the unit it protects and does not become a separate proof system.

*Why.* A check whose product is proof that another check ran creates another acceptance obligation without improving the requested result.

## A unit does not carry the deliverable

The rule above catches the code case, where plan and result are written in different media and the
altitude holds by itself. Where the deliverable is prose — documentation the task produces, briefs
for other agents, the answer of an investigation, a body of rules — plan and result share a medium
and nothing separates them by construction. The test that works in either medium: after the plan is
approved, work an intelligent executor still has to do remains, and a unit a later step could
satisfy by copying text out of the plan is a unit whose result is already written here.

*Why.* When the plan contains the result, the plan review reviews the result, the unit's own review
reads the same text a second time, and nothing has independently judged the work. The gates all
report green because each of them saw the artifact it was asked about; what none of them saw is the
step that was supposed to produce it.


## Development planning stops at the repository delivery boundary

A development unit may own implementation, tests, permanent documentation, generated and executable consequences, validation, review, and explicitly authorized project-native local commits or checkpoints. Push, pull request creation or merge, publication, release, and deployment stay with the caller or parent process and never become development-plan units. Authorized downstream intent remains visible in the final report until a standard parent-process handoff exists.

*Why.* Tool availability does not grant delivery authority, and mixing external delivery into implementation makes one workflow claim effects it neither validates nor owns.

## Each unit carries one visual policy and one approval policy

Every unit states visualMode as exactly disabled, screenshots, or html_report, and userApproval as true or false. html_report includes the same screenshot capture and actual inspection required by screenshots; it is not a second capture pass. In autonomous mode every userApproval is false. The intake preference guides plan construction only; after approval the current plan is the sole source of these policies.

*Why.* Separate screenshot and report booleans admit contradictory states, while a global preference or old unit index can silently override a revised plan.

engineering_standards.default:
# Engineering standards

These are outcomes, not procedures. An item that does not apply to the current change is met, and
nothing needs to be produced to prove it inapplicable. Cite only what is violated; do not walk this
document item by item.

## A module hides a decision, and its interface is smaller than what it does

The interface is everything a caller must know: signatures, ordering constraints, error behaviour,
guarantees. Judge a module by how much complexity it removes from everyone else, not by its size.

*Why.* A module whose interface is nearly as complicated as its implementation has moved code
without hiding anything. Making a unit slightly larger to hide a decision is usually the better
trade. (Deep modules; information hiding.)

## The same design decision is not reflected in two places

Two modules that must both know a format, an ordering, or a schema are one decision leaked across a
boundary, and the boundary is in the wrong place.

*Why.* Leaked decisions change together and are found separately. The classic source is decomposing
by the order things happen rather than by the knowledge each part holds. (Information leakage;
temporal decomposition.)

## A published interface is extended or versioned, never quietly changed

Where callers exist outside the change, the old behaviour keeps working while the new one is
introduced, and the removal window is stated. Where callers are all inside the change, they are
updated in the same change.

*Why.* Consumers depend on every observable behaviour, documented or not, so "nobody uses that" is a
claim to verify, not to assume — and a version number alone communicates nothing to them. (Hyrum's
Law; empirical studies find breaking changes as often in minor releases as in major ones.)

## Dependencies point inward, and there are no cycles

Domain logic does not know about transport, storage, or presentation; the outer layers depend on it.

*Why.* When the core knows about the edge, the edge cannot be replaced or tested, and a cycle makes
both ends impossible to reason about alone.

## Abstraction appears after repetition, not before it

A second similar case is evidence; an anticipated third is not.

*Why.* An abstraction built for imagined cases fits none of them well, and its cost — the indirection
every reader now traverses — is paid immediately while the benefit stays hypothetical.

## Effects and state live at the edges

The core is deterministic and reachable by tests without infrastructure.

*Why.* Logic entangled with I/O can only be exercised through the slowest path available, so it stops
being exercised.

## Errors are handled where there is a decision to make

Context is preserved on the way up; failures are not swallowed, and are not converted into a success
value that a caller cannot distinguish.

*Why.* A caught error with nowhere to go becomes an invisible wrong result later, and the place that
could have decided has lost the information it needed.

## Data and schema changes carry a path forward and a path back

Migration, and what happens to data written by the previous shape.

*Why.* The failure appears in production, on data nobody has in development.

## Security and performance are stated with the contract they constrain

Not appended afterwards as a review topic.

*Why.* A constraint discovered after the interface exists is either ignored or forces the interface
to be rebuilt.

## Follow the project's patterns by analogy — and do not replicate a defect

Find the places that already solve this kind of problem and follow them. Where the surrounding code
is wrong, implement correctly, say plainly where you diverged and why, and report the defect you
found rather than silently repairing unrelated areas.

*Why.* Consistency is what makes a codebase readable, but consistency with a defect multiplies it,
and an unannounced divergence looks like an accident to the next reader. Repairing what the task did
not ask for hides the actual change inside unrelated diffs.

## What you touch does not get worse

Dead code, debug leftovers, and TODOs standing in for delivery are removed from what the change
touches.

*Why.* Each is a claim about the code that is no longer true, and the cost of verifying it falls on
every later reader.


## Supporting validation does not become a second product

Add a validator, harness, adapter, or protocol only when its observation distinguishes relevant states and it has a consumer in the requested outcome. Do not create infrastructure whose purpose is proving that another check or report used the intended path.

*Why.* Recursive proof machinery adds coupling and acceptance obligations while leaving product behavior unchanged.

## Autonomy is bounded by useful work

Autonomy permits independent exploration, implementation, repair, and verification inside the user's outcome and authority. It does not authorize new criteria, platforms, or internal processes unrelated to that outcome.

*Why.* Extra mechanism is not progress merely because the agent can build it without asking.

test_standards.default:
# Test standards

These are outcomes, not procedures. An item that does not apply to the current change is met, and
nothing needs to be produced to prove it inapplicable. Cite only what is violated; do not walk this
document item by item.

## A test names the behaviour it protects and fails when that behaviour regresses

If no realistic defect makes it fail, it is not protecting anything.

*Why.* This is the property every other one serves: a suite that cannot fail for a behavioural reason
reports churn instead of regressions. (Test Desiderata — behavioural.)

## Tests exercise the public surface and assert state, not interactions

Reach the behaviour the way a caller reaches it. Assert what the system ends up being or returning,
not which internal calls happened in which order.

*Why.* Asserting interactions couples the test to the current implementation, so it fails on every
refactor that changes nothing observable — the change-detector test — and, worse, keeps passing when
a collaborator's real behaviour changes underneath. (Google: change-detector tests; test state, not
interactions.)

## A test does not assert what the compiler, type system, or linter already guarantees

That a field exists, that an argument has a type, that formatting holds.

*Why.* Such an assertion cannot fail for a behavioural reason — the earlier tool fails first — so it
adds maintenance without adding protection, and it makes the suite look stronger than it is. This
one is reasoning from the properties above rather than a citation; the literature names the adjacent
case, a test that re-implements the production algorithm to compare it with itself.

## No assertion that cannot fail, and none that might not run

An assertion inside a conditional the run may skip, a test with no assertion at all, or an expectation
that restates its input.

*Why.* All three report success without having checked anything, and they are indistinguishable from
real coverage in every report the project produces.

## Each level asserts its own responsibility

Unit for logic and boundaries, integration for the contract between components, end-to-end for the
user-visible path. The same behaviour is not asserted at three levels.

*Why.* Duplicated assertions multiply the cost of every change to that behaviour, and when they
disagree nobody knows which one states the intent.

## Tests are deterministic and independent of order

No dependence on wall-clock time, network, shared mutable state, or on another test having run first.

*Why.* A test that fails intermittently trains everyone to rerun rather than investigate, and it
takes real failures down with it. (Test Desiderata — isolated, deterministic.)

## A performance assertion carries a threshold that can fail

*Why.* A measurement without a bound records a number; it never reports a regression.

## The name states the condition and the expected outcome

Not the method under test.

*Why.* When it fails, the name is the whole diagnosis a reader gets before opening anything.

## Fixtures and helpers come from the project

Use the existing helpers, factories, and auth or setup utilities rather than building a parallel set.

*Why.* Parallel infrastructure drifts from the real setup, and its tests then pass against a world
the application does not live in.

## A defect is closed by a test that failed before the fix

*Why.* Otherwise nothing proves the fix addressed the reported behaviour, and the same defect can
return unnoticed.

## Coverage artifacts the project maintains are updated with the change

*Why.* A coverage map nobody updates stops describing the suite and starts misleading the next
author. Coverage percentage itself is not a quality criterion: it records that lines executed, not
that behaviour was checked. (SWE at Google, testing overview.)


## Evidence follows the property under test

Before adding a test helper, harness, adapter, guard, proxy, or metatest, name the required state, a plausible wrong state, and the observation that differs. A call, counter, token, or generated report does not prove semantic completeness or business provenance when the wrong state can produce the same signal. Use direct behavioral evidence or independent inspection instead.

*Why.* Mechanizing an indistinguishable property produces confidence without information and makes the harness itself the next thing to prove.

## A verification-only repair stays verification-only only while product truth is unchanged

Changed tests, fixtures, coverage evidence, or verification specifications may use a bounded validation cycle when product behavior, contracts, schemas, configuration, generated behavior, architecture, and test intent remain unchanged. If the new evidence exposes a product defect and repair reaches any of those sources, the product validation suffix becomes stale immediately.

*Why.* The place a repair started does not bound what it eventually changed.

## A requested validator is tested as a product

When validation machinery itself is the requested result, test its consumer-facing behavior and distinguishing output through the same product standards. Do not exempt it as infrastructure or require a second mechanism merely to prove the first mechanism ran.

*Why.* Product status follows the user's outcome, not the implementation category.

documentation_standards.default:
# Documentation standards

These are outcomes, not procedures. An item that does not apply to the current change is met, and
nothing needs to be produced to prove it inapplicable. Cite only what is violated; do not walk this
document item by item.

## Documentation describes the current state

No change history, no "previously", no announcements of what is new, no promises about what will
come.

*Why.* A reader arrives to learn how the system behaves now. History in a reference page makes them
reconstruct which sentence is still true, and the version control system already holds the history
properly.

## Every claim is checkable against the code, the configuration, or a command that runs

Examples work as written; commands are the ones the project actually has.

*Why.* One example that fails costs more trust than ten missing pages, and readers cannot tell a
stale example from a mistake of their own.

## Each page has one job

Teaching a newcomer, guiding someone through a task, stating facts to look up, or explaining why the
design is what it is. Knowing which one a page is tells you what belongs in it and what belongs
elsewhere.

*Why.* A page that mixes them serves nobody: the learner drowns in reference detail and the person
looking up a fact wades through narrative. This is a discipline for the author, not a required
directory layout — projects adopt it incrementally. (Diátaxis.)

## What is documented is the contract and the behaviour

Internal detail appears only where a reader must act on it.

*Why.* Documented internals become promises: readers depend on them, and changing them then breaks
people who followed the documentation.

## Placement and form follow the project

Match the structure, depth, and voice of the documentation that already exists; project style comes
first, house style second.

*Why.* Documentation is read as a set, not as pages; a page in a foreign format reads as an
afterthought regardless of its content. Style guides are guidance and yield to project style.
(Google developer documentation style guide.)

## Translations stay in parity where the project keeps more than one language

The same pages, the same structure, the same claims; a change lands in all of them or in none.

*Why.* A partially updated translation is worse than an untranslated one, because it states outdated
facts with the same authority as current ones.

## No new long-lived document without a durable reader

Update the page that already owns the subject.

*Why.* Documents accumulate faster than they are read; each new one splits the subject and makes the
next author guess which is authoritative.

## No numbers that drift

Counts of tests, tools, node types, or packages.

*Why.* They are wrong within weeks and nothing fails when they are, so they teach readers to distrust
the rest of the page.


## Permanent documentation closes with its vertical unit

The implementer updates every affected permanent document in the same unit as the behavior it describes, the fresh producer pass leaves the unit account true, and independent completeness review judges current documentation with code and tests. The final reconciliation still checks cross-unit truth, commands, links, generated output, and language parity, but an unchanged document with current independent unit coverage does not require a duplicate independent documentation review.

*Why.* Deferring obvious documentation makes review discover producer work, while reviewing unchanged already accepted documentation again adds a full loop without new evidence.

review_standards.description: Independent review, repair and evidence contract; materialized into the workspace by the engine
review_standards.default:
# Review, repair, and evidence

These are outcomes, not procedures. An item that does not apply to the current change is met, and
nothing needs to be produced to prove it inapplicable. Cite only what is violated; do not walk this
document item by item.

## Review

### Independence is required where the flow marks a review independent

Where a review is declared independent, whoever produced the artifact does not review it: a subagent
or a separate context is the usual way to obtain that, and where no such context is available, say so
plainly in the report rather than pretending the review was independent.

Where a flow judges a gate locally — the same agent, in the ordinary run — the obligation is
different and just as binding: judge from the primary sources rather than from your own account of
the work, and do not lower the bar because you wrote the thing. Do not manufacture independence a
local gate did not ask for; delegation costs a turn and a context, and the flow decides where to
spend it.

*Why.* The producer knows what they meant, so they read the intent instead of the artifact — which is
exactly the failure the review exists to catch. Reading the diff, the tests and the evidence instead
of your memory is what recovers most of that at a local gate; a flow buys a genuinely separate reader
where the risk justifies the cost.

### The reviewer reads the primary sources

The actual artifact, the requirements it answers to, the surrounding code — not the producer's
account of what it does.

*Why.* A summary carries the producer's assumptions forward, including the one that caused the defect.

### The subject is the unit's current state, not the round's increment

A gate judges what the unit is now, measured against the state the unit started from — not the diff
of the latest repair. A defect the current round did not introduce is still a defect of the unit.

*Why.* By the fifth round the latest diff is three lines, and judging those three lines passes a unit
whose rounds broke each other's work. Judging the increment also leaves a regression homeless: the
round that caused it is over, so no later gate owns it.

### The baseline the unit is judged against is stated once and reused

It is the previous unit's checkpoint where the project's version control provides one, otherwise the
state recorded when the unit began. Whichever it is, the unit's first iteration writes it down in a
line, and everything afterwards refers to that line.

*Why.* With no written baseline each reviewer picks its own, and the ones that pick the last
iteration are judging the increment while believing they judge the unit.

### Each round is judged on its own

Re-read the artifact instead of inheriting a conclusion from the previous round, including your own.
"This was fine last time" is not evidence that it is fine now.

*Why.* Carried-forward conclusions accumulate: what was checked in the first round is an assumption
by the fourth, and the repair that invalidated it is exactly the change nobody re-examined.

### The report holds the complete current set of confirmed findings

One known file, overwritten each time. Each finding gives its location, the contract it violates, the
consequence that follows, and what would resolve it. Outward, return only the aggregate disposition the routing needs: pass, repair, or replan; keep finding detail in the report.

*Why.* Findings revealed one per round turn a repair into a queue of surprises, and findings copied
into workflow context drift from the file that holds them.

### Zero findings is a valid and expected outcome

A reviewer that must produce something will find a naming preference.

*Why.* The reviewer's job is to decide whether the artifact is acceptable, and a search that continues
until something is found makes the loop about the reviewer rather than the work. (Google's reviewer
standard.)

### Blocking requires an observable consequence

Something must break, be lost, be unverifiable, or violate a stated requirement. Style, naming,
speculative robustness, and hypothetical future needs are worth saying and are not blocking; say so
when you raise them.

*Why.* The standard is that the change definitely improves the state of the system, not that it is
perfect — nothing worsens the system's health, and nothing waits for polish. Technical facts overrule
preferences, and where no rule exists, existing code wins over taste. (Google: improvement, not
perfection; the "Nit:" convention.)

### The reviewer diagnoses the work; it does not repair it and does not design machinery

No new fields, protocols, or layers proposed for robustness nobody asked for. The one thing a
reviewer may change is the run's own record, under the rule below.

*Why.* A reviewer that rewrites the artifact is no longer independent of it, and a reviewer that
designs is proposing work instead of proving a defect.

### A finding is about the delivered work, not about the run's bookkeeping

A finding names something wrong in what is being delivered: the code, the tests, the documentation the
project keeps, or the evidence that the work is what it claims to be. The reports, reviews and
accounts a run writes into its own workspace are not the delivery.

The question that separates the two is whether editing the record alone makes its statement true.
When it does — a number that no longer matches the tree, a paragraph left standing after the change it
described was undone — whoever notices corrects that file where it stands, says so in their own
report, and raises no finding. When it does not, because the statement can only be made true by
changing the repository, it is a finding like any other: a record claiming work that was never done
hides work that was never done.

A reader whose role is to judge the delivery corrects records and never touches the repository; that
boundary is what keeps it independent of what it judges.

*Why.* A stale record is a two-line edit, and routing it as a finding buys the whole validation chain
for it — the cost that teaches a run to batch findings and an author to delete gates. What the record
protects is the reader who comes next, and that reader is served by the correction plus a sentence
saying it was wrong, not by a repair round.

### A delegated reviewer does not repeat mechanical checks whose evidence is current

Linters, type checks, test suites, and builds have already run.

*Why.* Rerunning them consumes the review turn on evidence that already exists and displaces the
judgement only a reviewer can supply.

## Repair

### The repair owner reproduces the defect before changing anything

*Why.* A fix aimed at a finding nobody reproduced usually changes something adjacent and leaves the
defect in place.

### A finding that cannot be reproduced is reported as such

With what was tried. It is not silently closed, and it does not start another identical round.

*Why.* An unchanged repeat costs a full cycle and produces the same report; the disagreement between
reviewer and repair owner is the actual finding at that point.

### The changed artifact returns to the same reviewer

*Why.* A second reviewer re-derives the context and finds a different set, so nothing ever converges.

## Evidence

### Evidence is what another person can reproduce

A command and its output, an inspected artifact, an observed state. Not a claim that something works.

*Why.* "Verified" without a trace is indistinguishable from unverified, and the run that has to be
resumed later cannot tell them apart either.

### A report states what the work delivers, not how much of it there was

The subject of a report is the outcome and the evidence for it. A number belongs in it when the
number is the deliverable, or is itself the output of a check that can fail — a test run, the count
of source remarks closed, a revision identifier. A number that measures the volume of the work —
files touched, lines added or removed, share of comment, percent reduced — is neither, and it is not
written.

*Why.* Reproducibility makes size the easiest number to produce, and nothing fails when a size number
drifts, so nothing keeps it true. Written down it is still a claim: the reviewer has to verify it and
the repair owner has to maintain it, which spends a round of review and a round of repair on a figure
that protects nothing.

### The account of the work is kept current by whoever last changed the work

Where a flow keeps a durable account of what the work now delivers, that account has one address, and
the responsibility that last changed the work leaves it true in the same turn. It is rewritten to
describe the present state, not appended to with the history of the rounds — the record of a round
is the round's own report.

*Why.* Gates and reviewers judge the current state. An account frozen at the first round disagrees
with the artifact by construction, and the disagreement surfaces as a review finding, so the round is
spent reconciling a description instead of judging the work.

### A change makes stale the evidence covering what it could have touched

That surface is re-established; evidence the change could not reach stays current, and which is which
is said rather than assumed. Deliberate before-and-after comparison keeps the earlier evidence on
purpose — that is not staleness.

*Why.* Treating every repair as invalidating everything makes each round cost a full revalidation,
which is how gates start being skipped wholesale; treating nothing as invalidated ships a unit whose
last change was never checked.

### An artifact's existence is not evidence it was inspected

Where visual acceptance matters, the images are opened and compared against expected behaviour; a
file on disk proves only that a file was produced.

*Why.* Capture that nobody looked at reliably passes while showing the wrong screen.

### An inapplicable check is recorded as inapplicable, with the reason

It is neither silently skipped nor reported as passed.

*Why.* A skipped check that reads as green is the one nobody revisits when the situation changes.

### Partial and failed results are reported as partial and failed

*Why.* A run reported as green on partial evidence moves the discovery of the failure to whoever
depends on it next, with less context than you have now.

## Cause is classified before repair

Classify every confirmed finding by its earliest cause: product defect, test or validation defect, insufficient existing evidence, documentation or process projection, invalid or undemonstrable criterion, or upstream requirements, plan, or process defect. Repair is valid only when every current blocker is owned by the reviewed artifact and its upstream contract is sound. An upstream, criterion, evidence-model, or mixed cause returns replan.

*Why.* The gate that noticed a problem does not necessarily own the source that must change.

## Replan preserves the requirement

Replan corrects a derived plan, architecture decision, criterion, or evidence method while preserving the user's original goal, authority, still-valid requirements, and completed outcomes. A change to the original task boundary still requires the user.

*Why.* A bad plan is not protected by scope, but implementation difficulty is not permission to lower the bar.

## A repeated root requires changed knowledge

After one substantive repair, the same root class cannot authorize another mutation unless a relevant source of truth, external fact, distinguishing observation, or testable hypothesis changed. Changed bytes, another guard, or a larger report are not changed knowledge. Reassess the plan, criterion, and evidence model instead.

*Why.* Repeating a mechanism that cannot distinguish success produces an unbounded validation loop.

## Validation-only drift stops before another mutation

When requested product evidence is green and consecutive attempts change only validation, reporting, harness, or acceptance machinery, reassess whether the criterion is demonstrable and whether the machinery has independent product value. Continue only with a stronger distinguishing observation or when validation is itself the requested result.

*Why.* Process machinery can grow indefinitely while the user's result does not change.

## Class-wide means bounded real manifestations

Establish a shared violated contract or root, define the original-task boundary, and inspect every materially analogous real manifestation inside it. Repair confirmed occurrences coherently. Do not build a universal detector for a contextual semantic or architectural property; use bounded primary-artifact inspection and review when no reliable mechanical observation exists.

*Why.* A class is defined by confirmed cause and scope, not by every place a new scanner could run.
